free_tier.stated: 10 databases; 500 MB per database; 5 GB per account; 5 million rows read per day; 100,000 rows written per day

per_object_cap.stated: 2,000,000 bytes per row, BLOB or string; 500 MB per database

retention.stated: data is kept until it is deleted; at the included 5 GB storage limit D1 blocks inserts, table changes and index creation until data is deleted
retention.notes: the null is indefinite: no deletion clock is published; the daily read and write limits reset at 00:00 UTC and refuse queries with an error until then, and the storage limit refuses inserts, table changes and index creation until data is deleted

egress.terms: no egress charge; rows read and rows written are the metered quantities

chaining: per-tenant SQLite in a Worker with a free Postgres as the system of record; 500 MB per database and 10 databases is 5 GB of free relational state

notes: The 100,000 rows written a day is the binding number for any ingest, and it is small: 1.16 rows a second sustained. A full table scan counts every row it scans as a row read, so an unindexed query spends the read budget fast.
